free_tier.stated: 1 TB of free storage per user, announced 2026-06-26, 'made possible through a National Science Foundation Campus Cyberinfrastructure grant' and backed by the Open Storage Network. Additional storage $200/TB one-time. 550 files max per record.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Unmetered egress. Downloads stream directly from data.caltech.edu. Storage resides on the Open Storage Network, an NSF-funded academic infrastructure fabric.

tooling: InvenioRDM REST API (/api/records, files under /api/records/<id>/files/<key>/content); purpose-built client caltechlibrary/caltechdata_api (github.com/caltechlibrary/caltechdata_api, 13 stars); the whole instance's source is public at caltechlibrary/caltechdata (11 stars) so the quota config is auditable
chaining: Default allocation is 1 TB free per registered institutional user. Deposited records are not individually account-capped, providing higher baseline capacity than general repositories.
limits_note: 550 files per record; deposit requires a Caltech (access.caltech) identity, which is the real gate. The API reads are fully anonymous but writes are not open to the public.

extras.quota_verbatim: 1 TB of free storage per user, announced 2026-06-26, 'made possible through a National Science Foundation Campus Cyberinfrastructure grant' and backed by the Open Storage Network. Additional storage $200/TB one-time. 550 files max per record.

extras.chaining_verbatim: 1 TB is the largest single free allocation I found in this niche and it is per user, not per record.
